name: Warhammer 40,000
description: Warhammer 40,000 is the dominant sci-fi tabletop wargame, pitting Space Marines, Chaos forces, Orks, Eldar, and dozens of other factions against each other in the 41st millennium. Modern kits since 2017 (Primaris range) sit squarely at 32mm heroic scale, while older Firstborn models measure closer to 28mm true scale.
scaleNotes: Games Workshop uses heroic proportions — heads, hands, and weapons are intentionally oversized so details read at arm's length. A Primaris Space Marine stands roughly 32mm to eye level, while a Firstborn Marine measures about 28mm. Mixing the two on the same table is noticeable but acceptable for casual play.
printingTips: 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm layer height gives the best facial detail on infantry. Rank-and-file units print well at 0.4mm nozzle and 0.08mm layers. Vehicles and terrain tolerate 0.12mm layers without visible quality loss. Orient character models upright; vehicles can be printed at 45° for fewer supports.
popularWith: Competitive wargamers, lore enthusiasts, army builders, and the largest 3D printing community for proxy miniatures.

name: Warhammer Age of Sigmar
description: Age of Sigmar replaced Warhammer Fantasy Battle in 2015, shifting from ranked infantry blocks to hero-focused skirmish and mass battle in a high-fantasy setting. The miniature scale matches modern Warhammer 40k — all new GW fantasy releases since 2015 are 32mm heroic.
scaleNotes: AoS uses the same 32mm heroic scale as Warhammer 40k Primaris. Older Warhammer Fantasy miniatures (pre-2015) were 28mm heroic and remain usable in Age of Sigmar and The Old World, though they sit slightly shorter than modern sculpts.
printingTips: AoS models tend to have dramatic poses with flowing cloaks and extended weapons. Print character models with 0.2mm nozzle for crisp edges on armor and chainmail. Large centerpiece models (Morrknul, Nagash) benefit from 0.04-0.06mm layers on resin. FDM works well for terrain and monsters at 0.1mm layers.
popularWith: Fantasy painters, narrative gamers, centerpiece collectors, and players who enjoy assembling painted armies for display.

name: Warhammer: The Old World
description: The Old World revives the classic Warhammer Fantasy setting with ranked regiments, tile-based movement, and the Old World map. It uses the legacy 28mm fantasy scale, making it compatible with decades of classic Citadel miniatures alongside new releases.
scaleNotes: The Old World deliberately returns to 28mm scale for its new plastic kits, matching the original Warhammer Fantasy range. This is smaller than Age of Sigmar's 32mm, so mixing the two ranges on the same table produces a visible size difference.
printingTips: Ranked regiment models work best printed in batches with consistent layer heights. 0.4mm nozzle at 0.08mm layers balances speed and detail for infantry blocks. Character models and unit champions benefit from 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm. Cavalry and chariots print well at 45° angle to minimize support scarring on horses.
popularWith: Veteran Warhammer Fantasy players, historical fantasy fans, and painters who enjoy ranked regiment displays.

name: Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game
description: Based on The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit films, MESBG is a skirmish-focused wargame where individual heroes matter as much as armies. The range spans from 25mm (older metal sculpts from the early 2000s) to modern 28mm plastic kits, all designed to match the film actors' proportions.
scaleNotes: MESBG occupies a unique position — older metal miniatures from the original Lord of the Rings range measure closer to 25mm, while newer plastic releases are 28mm. Both are used in the same game, and the size difference is accepted as part of the range's history.
printingTips: MESBG miniatures emphasize realistic proportions over heroic bulk. Print at 0.2mm nozzle and 0.06mm layers for best facial detail — many characters are based on specific actors and recognizable faces matter. Metal miniatures from the range are often thinner than plastics, so consider scaling up by 2-3% when replacing metal with printed alternatives.
popularWith: Tolkien fans, narrative skirmish players, film-accurate painters, and collectors who value character over army scale.

name: Bolt Action
description: Bolt Action is the most popular WWII tabletop wargame, covering platoon-level engagements from 1939-1945. Infantry are 28mm true scale (1:56), and vehicle kits from Warlord and other manufacturers follow the same ratio, making 1:35 model kit vehicles usable after slight downsizing.
scaleNotes: Bolt Action uses 28mm true scale — realistic human proportions with no heroic exaggeration. A standard infantryman measures 28mm from foot to eye level. Vehicle scale is 1:56, which aligns naturally with 28mm figures. Historical accuracy matters more here than in fantasy games.
printingTips: Historical miniatures reward accuracy over drama. Print infantry at 0.4mm nozzle and 0.08mm layers for rank-and-file, 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm for officers and snipers. Vehicles printed at 0.2mm layers look good on the table. Use reference photos of actual uniforms — players notice correct webbing and helmet shapes.
popularWith: History buffs, WWII enthusiasts, diorama builders, and players who enjoy research-backed army composition.

name: Dungeons & Dragons
description: Dungeons & Dragons is the original tabletop roleplaying game, where players create characters and embark on collaborative storytelling adventures. Miniatures are optional but widely used for combat encounters, with a Medium creature (human-sized) typically measuring 28mm to eye level on a 175cm baseline.
scaleNotes: D&D miniatures span an enormous range — a Tiny rat might be 10mm while a Gargantuan ancient dragon can exceed 150mm. The baseline for a Medium humanoid is 28mm true scale. Official WotC miniatures from the Nolzur's and Icons lines are 28mm, though many 3D printed alternatives are designed at 32mm for better detail.
printingTips: D&D demands variety — a single session might need goblins, dragons, and dungeon tiles. Print怪物 at 0.4mm nozzle and 0.1mm layers for speed, hero characters at 0.2mm and 0.06mm for detail. FDM is excellent for terrain and large monsters; resin shines for character models with fine details like spell effects and flowing robes.
popularWith: Dungeon Masters building encounter collections, players wanting personalized hero minis, and the largest single market for 3D printed tabletop figures.

name: Star Wars: Legion
description: Star Wars: Legion is a rank-and-file mass battle game set in the Star Wars universe, covering the Original Trilogy and beyond. Miniatures are measured at 35mm eye level (1:47 scale), making them noticeably larger than Warhammer 40k but smaller than Shatterpoint.
scaleNotes: Legion's 35mm designation refers to eye-level measurement — a Stormtrooper's eyes sit 35.7mm above the base. The full figure (top of helmet) reaches about 40mm. This is 1:47 scale based on a 1678mm eye-height reference. Bandai and Revell sell compatible Star Wars kits at 1:48 scale.
printingTips: Legion miniatures have smooth armor surfaces that show layer lines easily. Print at 0.06mm layers or finer for Stormtroopers and Clone Troopers. Vehicles (AT-ST, AT-RT) print well on FDM at 0.1mm layers. Use the chain-link lock in your slicer to maintain proportions when scaling STLs from other systems.
popularWith: Star Wars fans, cinematic battle players, and hobbyists who enjoy painting iconic film characters.

name: Star Wars: Shatterpoint
description: Shatterpoint is a squad-based skirmish game where each player commands a small team of named Star Wars characters. The 40mm scale was chosen specifically to capture high-resolution detail while providing large, smooth surfaces ideal for painters practicing blending techniques.
scaleNotes: At 40mm, Shatterpoint miniatures are the largest standard Star Wars game scale. Atomic Mass Games chose this size to give painters expansive surfaces for blending and highlighting — a deliberate departure from the smaller scales used in Legion and MCP. Characters like Dooku measure approximately 42.75mm total height.
printingTips: The large, smooth surfaces of Shatterpoint minis reward fine layer heights — print at 0.04-0.06mm on resin for best results. FDM at 0.08mm is acceptable for terrain pieces. The bigger scale means more material per model, so factor resin usage into your cost calculations. Orient helmets and faces carefully to minimize support marks on visible areas.
popularWith: Star Wars painters who want larger canvases, skirmish gamers, and collectors building diorama-style displays.

name: Marvel: Crisis Protocol
description: Marvel: Crisis Protocol pits Marvel superheroes and villains against each other in cinematic tabletop battles. The game uses 35mm true scale with realistic proportions — no heroic exaggeration — making the miniatures notably larger and more detailed than Warhammer-scale equivalents.
scaleNotes: MCP uses true-scale 35mm proportions, meaning characters look like realistic humans at that size rather than the exaggerated heroic proportions of 32mm GW miniatures. Larger characters (Hulk, Thanos) come on bigger bases but maintain consistent scale with standard characters.
printingTips: MCP miniatures feature dynamic superhero poses with flowing capes and energy effects. Print at 0.2mm nozzle and 0.06mm layers for character models. The larger scale means fewer visible layer lines at standard settings compared to 28mm. Terrain pieces (cars, lampposts, rubble) print excellently on FDM at 0.1mm layers.
popularWith: Marvel fans, cinematic skirmish players, and painters who enjoy vibrant comic-book color schemes.

name: Malifaux
description: Malifaux is a card-driven skirmish game set in a gothic steampunk alternate Earth where magic and technology collide. Miniatures are 32mm heroic scale, produced in high-quality plastic since the 4th Edition relaunch, with a distinctive artistic style that blends horror, western, and Victorian aesthetics.
scaleNotes: Malifaux miniatures are 32mm heroic scale — compatible in size with modern Warhammer 40k and Age of Sigmar. The artistic style is more exaggerated than GW, with larger heads and more expressive faces designed to convey character personality at tabletop distance.
printingTips: Malifaux miniatures are known for expressive faces and intricate clothing details. Use 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm layers for the best results on character models. The 4th Edition plastic range is well-suited for kitbashing with 3D printed alternative parts. Resin printing is strongly recommended for this range due to the fine detail on accessories and weapons.
popularWith: Gothic aesthetic enthusiasts, competitive skirmish players, and painters who enjoy dramatic color palettes and weathering effects.

name: Infinity
description: Infinity is a Japanese-anime-influenced sci-fi skirmish game set in a far-future human sphere. Corvus Belli's metal miniatures are renowned for their dynamic poses and intricate detail, with slimmer proportions than heroic-scale games despite the 28mm designation.
scaleNotes: Infinity models are nominally 28mm but measure closer to 29-30mm in practice due to scale creep across the range. The proportions are leaner and more realistic than heroic 28mm — heads and hands are smaller relative to body size. This gives Infinity a distinctly different visual feel from Warhammer despite the overlapping scale numbers.
printingTips: Infinity models are famous for thin weapons, flowing hair, and delicate equipment — all challenging for FDM. Resin printing is strongly recommended. Use 0.2mm nozzle at 0.04-0.06mm layers for best results. Support placement is critical — attach supports to hidden areas like undersides and backs. Printed alternatives often need to be scaled up 5-10% to match official Corvus Belli metal minis.
popularWith: Tactical skirmish players, anime aesthetic fans, and painters who enjoy NMM (non-metallic metal) techniques on sci-fi armor.

name: Warmachine & Hordes
description: Warmachine and its companion game Hordes pit steam-powered warjacks and magical beasts against each other in a fantasy world of industrial warfare. Originally labelled 28mm, Privateer Press shifted to calling the scale 30mm as the range evolved through scale creep.
scaleNotes: Warmachine was originally marketed as 28mm but was reclassified to 30mm around the time Hordes launched. The miniatures are compatible in size with 28mm heroic ranges — the difference is subtle enough that mixing on the same table is common in casual play.
printingTips: Warmachine models feature bulky, mechanical designs — warjacks and heavy beasts have flat armor panels that show layer lines. Print at 0.06mm layers on resin or 0.08mm on FDM. The chunky proportions are forgiving for FDM printing. Metal originals are heavy, so printed resin alternatives are significantly lighter and easier to transport.
popularWith: Competitive tournament players, steampunk enthusiasts, and gamers who enjoy complex army synergies and control-point mechanics.

name: Frostgrave & Stargrave
description: Frostgrave is a fantasy skirmish game about wizards exploring a frozen ruined city, while Stargrave applies the same system to a sci-fi setting. Both are miniature-agnostic — you can use any 28mm fantasy or sci-fi figures, making them ideal for 3D printing custom warbands.
scaleNotes: Frostgrave official miniatures (produced by Warlord Games) are 28mm true scale. The game is explicitly miniature-agnostic, so any 28mm or 32mm figures work. Stargrave leans toward 28mm sci-fi but accepts the same range. This flexibility makes both games a natural fit for 3D printed collections.
printingTips: Because Frostgrave/Stargrave are miniature-agnostic, you can print anything — this is one of the best games for 3D printing experimentation. Print warbands in batches at 0.4mm nozzle and 0.08mm layers for playability. Characters and wizards benefit from 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm. Terrain (frozen ruins, sci-fi corridors) is a major part of the game and prints well on FDM.
popularWith: Solo and small-group gamers, 3D printing enthusiasts, kitbashers, and players who enjoy building thematic warbands from mixed sources.

name: Kings of War
description: Kings of War is Mantic Games' rank-and-flank fantasy wargame, designed as an alternative to Warhammer Fantasy with streamlined rules and regiment-based play. The entire range is 28mm scale, and the game actively encourages using miniatures from any fantasy range.
scaleNotes: Kings of War uses standard 28mm fantasy scale. Mantic's own miniatures are slightly smaller than Games Workshop's heroic 28mm, but the difference is minimal on the table. The game's regiment-based movement system means individual miniature scale matters less than unit footprint.
printingTips: Kings of War rewards mass production — you need entire regiments, not single characters. Print infantry in large batches at 0.4mm nozzle and 0.1mm layers for speed. Mantic's regiment movement trays can be 3D printed easily. Focus print quality on unit champions and characters; rank-and-file troops are viewed from 4+ feet away.
popularWith: Mass battle fantasy gamers, regiment painters, and players seeking a streamlined alternative to rank-and-flank systems.

name: BattleTech
description: BattleTech is a tactical wargame where players control giant robotic war machines called BattleMechs. Miniatures are 6mm scale (approximately 1:285), with 'mechs ranging from 30mm to 55mm tall depending on weight class. The game uses hex-movement rather than measuring tapes.
scaleNotes: BattleTech 'mechs represent machines 9-15 meters tall. At 1:285 scale, a 12-meter 'mech should be about 42mm tall, but actual miniatures vary widely — Catalyst's modern sculpts are closer to 1:265 (slightly larger than true 1:285). Older Iron Wind Metals miniatures are smaller and closer to the original ratio. Scale consistency within the range matters more than mathematical accuracy.
printingTips: BattleTech miniatures are small but detailed — cockpit glass, weapon barrels, and antenna all need to read clearly. Print at 0.2mm nozzle and 0.04-0.06mm layers on resin for best results. FDM struggles at this scale; use it only for terrain and hex tiles. Magnetize bases for transport — small models shift easily in cases.
popularWith: Tactical wargamers, mech enthusiasts, retro sci-fi fans, and players who enjoy deep customization of individual units.

name: Flames of War
description: Flames of War is the leading 15mm WWII wargame, covering company-level engagements across all major theaters. Miniatures are 1:100 scale, allowing entire companies with supporting armor to fit on a standard gaming table. Team Yankee extends the system to Cold War-era conflicts.
scaleNotes: At 15mm (1:100), Flames of War miniatures are small enough to field dozens of vehicles and hundreds of infantry on a single table. The scale is close to but not identical to 1:100 model kits — Battlefront's figures are slightly larger than strict ratio scale to improve tabletop readability.
printingTips: 15mm miniatures reward batch printing — you need entire platoons. Print at 0.2mm nozzle and 0.06mm layers on resin for infantry; FDM at 0.08mm works for vehicles and terrain. Magnetize vehicle bases for transport. The small scale means painting is faster but basing (flocking, static grass) has a proportionally larger visual impact.
popularWith: WWII history enthusiasts, company-level tactical gamers, and players who enjoy painting large collections of vehicles and infantry.

name: Dropzone Commander
description: Dropzone Commander is a 10mm sci-fi wargame depicting massive 27th-century battles with infantry, tanks, and dropships. The small scale allows entire companies with transport vehicles to be fielded in a single game, emphasizing combined-arms tactics over individual heroics.
scaleNotes: At 10mm, individual infantry figures are barely larger than a grain of rice. The game's visual impact comes from vehicle mass and formation density rather than individual detail. TTCombat's range is consistent within itself, making cross-faction mixing straightforward.
printingTips: 10mm miniatures are small enough that FDM struggles with infantry — resin is strongly recommended. Print at 0.2mm nozzle and 0.04mm layers. Vehicles are the stars of this game and print well on FDM at 0.06mm layers. Use a single base color for infantry to maintain visual cohesion across the table.
popularWith: Mass battle sci-fi gamers, combined-arms tacticians, and players who prefer vehicle-heavy armies over individual character focus.

name: Legions Imperialis
description: Legions Imperialis is Games Workshop's return to epic-scale warfare, covering the Horus Heresy with hundreds of miniatures on a single table. At 8mm, individual Space Marines are tiny but recognizable, and Titans loom over entire formations.
scaleNotes: Legions Imperialis uses 8mm scale, matching the older Adeptus Titanicus range. The scale is designed so that a Titan miniature is roughly the same physical size as a 28mm infantry model, creating an intentionally dramatic size contrast on the table.
printingTips: At 8mm, resin printing is essential for infantry — FDM cannot reliably produce details at this scale. Print at 0.2mm nozzle and 0.04mm layers. Vehicles and Titans are larger and more forgiving. Use contrast paints or washes heavily — at this scale, speed-painting techniques are more practical than layering.
popularWith: Epic-scale enthusiasts, Horus Heresy lore fans, and players who enjoy commanding massive formations rather than individual squads.

name: Grimdark Future (One Page Rules)
description: Grimdark Future is One Page Rules' free, miniature-agnostic sci-fi wargame — a streamlined alternative to Warhammer 40k that works with any 28-32mm miniatures. The rules fit on a single page, and the game explicitly encourages using 3D printed, proxy, or converted models.
scaleNotes: Grimdark Future has no official miniature range — it is designed to work with whatever you own. The 32mm recommendation aligns with modern Games Workshop and the majority of 3D printed STL files. The game's flexibility makes it the most accessible entry point for players with custom-printed collections.
printingTips: Grimdark Future is the ideal game for 3D printing — there are no official models to match, so print whatever you want. Use the game's base size chart to ensure your printed models fit the correct base categories. The forgiving rule system means visual consistency matters less than having the right base size.
popularWith: 3D printing enthusiasts, rules-light gamers, proxy army builders, and players who want Warhammer-style gameplay without the cost of official miniatures.

name: Fallout: Wasteland Warfare
description: Fallout: Wasteland Warfare brings the Fallout video game universe to the tabletop with 32mm miniatures covering factions like the Brotherhood of Steel, NCR, Raiders, and Super Mutants. The game supports both PvP and solo/cooperative play against AI-driven encounters.
scaleNotes: All Fallout: Wasteland Warfare miniatures are 32mm scale, matching modern Warhammer and Malifaux. The range includes both pre-assembled PVC miniatures (starter sets) and multi-part resin kits for hobbyists. Creature models like Deathclaws are significantly larger but maintain consistent scale.
printingTips: Fallout miniatures benefit from weathering and rust effects that hide layer lines naturally. Print at 0.2mm nozzle and 0.06mm layers for characters, 0.08mm for Power Armor suits. The post-apocalyptic aesthetic is forgiving — damaged and rough surfaces are thematically appropriate. Terrain (ruined buildings, vehicles) is a major component and prints well on FDM.
popularWith: Fallout video game fans, solo/cooperative gamers, narrative players, and painters who enjoy weathering and environmental storytelling.

name: Gaslands
description: Gaslands is a post-apocalyptic vehicular combat game that uses modified Hot Wheels and Matchbox cars as miniatures. At 1:56 scale, these die-cast cars are compatible with 28mm infantry, making it easy to add foot soldiers, terrain, and custom 3D printed accessories.
scaleNotes: Gaslands vehicles are 1:56 scale die-cast cars — the same ratio as 28mm infantry. This natural compatibility means 3D printed weapon mounts, armor plates, and terrain pieces designed for 28mm work perfectly. The game uses template-based movement rather than measuring tape.
printingTips: Gaslands is a 3D printing playground — weapon mounts, roll cages, spike strips, and terrain scatter all print beautifully. Use 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm layers for weapon details. Print accessories in resin for durability, terrain in FDM for speed. The game encourages creative kitbashing over precision painting.
popularWith: Kitbashers, die-cast car modifiers, post-apocalyptic enthusiasts, and players who enjoy creative modeling over strict historical accuracy.
